rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Matter is a swarm of molecules: ~10²³ of them per mole ($N_A = 6.022\times10^{23}$), each ~10⁻¹⁰ m across, attracting strongly at close range and repelling fiercely below that. The **state of matter** is set by spacing and force balance: solids vibrate about fixed lattice sites (fixed shape), liquids slide past neighbours (fixed volume, fluid shape), gases fly nearly freely through ~10× wider spaces (compressible,…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - n = m/M; N = nN_A - N_A = 6.022×10²³ /mol - Loschmidt number ≈ 2.7×10¹⁹ /cm³ at STP

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **State-Dependent Molecular Spacing:** In gases, intermolecular spacing $\gg$ molecular diameter ($\sim 10\times$); in liquids, spacing $\approx$ molecular diameter; in solids, molecules are locked in a lattice. This spacing determines the dominant energy (KE in gases, PE in solids) and compressibility.  ·  **Intermolecular vs Intramolecular Forces:** Intermolecular forces (van der Waals, H-bonding, dipole-dipole) are weak ($\sim 1-100$ kJ/mol) and govern phase changes. Intramolecular (chemical) bonds are strong ($\sim 100-1000$ kJ/mol) and govern molecular structure. Phase transitions break intermolecular bonds, not intramolecular ones.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Matter is composed of a large number of molecules separated by spaces and held by intermolecular forces."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***One drop of water*** — ~10²¹ molecules, each ~3×10⁻¹⁰ m across.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Moles vs molecules:** divide mass by molar mass to get moles; multiply by N_A to get molecules.  ·  **Diatomic masses:** H₂ is 2 g/mol, O₂ is 32 g/mol — count both atoms.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Matter Made of Molecules Everything around you is a swarm of molecules: in solids they vibrate in place, in liquids they slide past each other, in gases they fly freely. Molecular properties — size, number, spacing, intermolecular forces — explain the three states of matter from one picture.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Molecular picture of matter - Matter consists of a very large number of molecules ($N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$ per mole) separated by spaces. - Molecules attract each other with forces that vary strongly with separation: negligible far apart, strong at close range (attractive, then strongly repulsive below ~10⁻¹⁰ m).…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (2m): Find the number of molecules in 4 g of oxygen (O₂, M = 32 g/mol).** — n = 4/32 = 0.125 mol → N = 0.125 × 6.022×10²³ = 7.5×10²² molecules.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **One picture, three states:** spacing and force strength explain every macroscopic difference.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Matter = many molecules + spacing + intermolecular forces + ceaseless motion.  ·  Solids vibrate; liquids slide; gases fly freely.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Air molecules at STP travel a mean free path of ~68 nm between collisions — colliding ~10⁹ times per second.
